newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU panel to meet on Franco-German EMU plans.
newsitem.headline: EU panel to meet on Franco-German EMU plans.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee will hold a scheduled meeting on Wednesday to discuss French and German economic convergence programmes to qualify for the European single currency, monetary officials said.
The two programmes reassert France's and Germany's commitment to sound public finances to remain on track for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), one official said.

Paris and Bonn recently updated their convergence programmes following a request by the European Commission which must decide in early 1998 which EU countries can participate in the single currency, the euro, based on their 1997 economic performance.
EU finance ministers will in turn discuss the plans at their next scheduled meeting on March 17.
France is expecting to cut its budget deficit to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 and 2.8 percent in 1998 from 4.0 percent in 1996.

Germany is also determined to slash its deficit to 2.9 percent in 1997 from 3.9 percent in 1996, but many economists see it clearly over the three-percent threshold set in the Maastricht treaty on Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Italy and Portugal, whose plans have also been judged outdated, have still to submit revised plans. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
